record.original_question: How should the notions of general fractional integrals and general fractional derivatives, originally developed on the positive real semi-axis using Sonine-type kernels and convolution formulas, be adapted to functions defined on a finite interval and on the whole real line R?

evidence.quote: Now we introduce the general fractional integrals and derivatives of arbitrary (non-integer) order and discuss some of their basic properties (for more properties and examples see [40]).
Adjust the notions of the GFIs and GFDs to the case of a finite interval and R.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. A pair of locally integrable functions $\kappa,k:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ is called a Sonine pair if their Laplace convolution satisfies
$$(\kappa * k)(t)=\int_0^t \kappa(t-\tau)\,k(\tau)\,d\tau = 1, \qquad t>0.$$
For such a pair, the general fractional integral (GFI) and the general fractional derivative (GFD) of a function $f:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ are defined, on the positive real semi-axis, by
$$(\mathbb{I}_{(\kappa)} f)(t) = \int_0^t \kappa(t-\tau)\,f(\tau)\,d\tau,$$
$$(\mathbb{D}_{(k)} f)(t) = \frac{d}{dt}\int_0^t k(t-\tau)\,f(\tau)\,d\tau \qquad\text{(Riemann–Liouville type)},$$
$$({}_*\mathbb{D}_{(k)} f)(t) = \int_0^t k(t-\tau)\,f'(\tau)\,d\tau \qquad\text{(Caputo type)}.$$
The Sonine condition $(\kappa*k)(t)=1$ guarantees the fundamental identities $\mathbb{D}_{(k)}\mathbb{I}_{(\kappa)} f = f$ and analogous projector formulas. Definitions for arbitrary (non-integer) order are obtained by iterating or extending these constructions to suitable kernel classes.

Problem. Develop a consistent theory of general fractional integrals and general fractional derivatives, with Sonine-type kernels and convolution structure as above, in the following two settings, in such a way that the Sonine pairing, the fundamental theorems of fractional calculus (left- and right-inverse relations between GFI and GFD), the projector formulas, and appropriate function spaces on which the operators act, are all preserved:

(a) Functions defined on a finite interval $[a,b]\subset\mathbb{R}$: define left-sided and right-sided GFIs and GFDs on $[a,b]$, identify the admissible kernel classes, and establish their mapping properties and inversion relations.

(b) Functions defined on the whole real line $\mathbb{R}$: define two-sided (left, right, and Liouville/Marchaut-type) GFIs and GFDs on $\mathbb{R}$, identify the admissible kernel classes (including Fourier-analytic characterizations of the Sonine condition), and establish their mapping properties and inversion relations.
artifact.category_tag: general fractional calculus with Sonine kernels
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work in general fractional calculus has introduced GFIs/GFDs on finite intervals (e.g., right-sided operators, multi-kernel approach, 1st-level GFDs) and partial extensions, but a complete, unified theory adapting the Sonine-kernel GFI/GFD framework to both finite intervals and to the whole real line (with two-sided/Liouville-type operators and full inversion theorems) does not appear to have been fully established. The problem appears to be partially addressed rather than fully solved.

status_evidence.title: General Fractional Integrals and Derivatives of Arbitrary Order
status_evidence.snippet: GFIs and GFDs considered so far have been defined for functions on the real positive semi-axis.
status_evidence.claim: Original framework is on the positive semi-axis.

status_evidence.title: General Fractional Calculus: Multi-Kernel Approach
status_evidence.snippet: Extensions of GFI/GFD via multi-kernel approach.
status_evidence.claim: Partial extensions of the framework exist but not a complete finite-interval/whole-line theory.

status_evidence.title: The 1st Level General Fractional Derivatives and Some of Their Properties
status_evidence.snippet: Further development of GFDs in the Sonine-kernel framework.
status_evidence.claim: Continued development of GFD theory, still primarily on the semi-axis.
